notes.author: user
notes.text: Pass project-specific parameters to a managed dev server generically; WinPath's E2E reset configuration is the motivating example.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: WinPath uses environment variables such as E2E_RESET_DB_CONFIRM, PLAYWRIGHT_E2E_RESET_SECRET, PLAYWRIGHT_E2E_DB_LAB, and GOOGLE_CALENDAR_E2E_FIXTURES. Model this primarily as typed environment overrides and profiles, not shell text appended to a command.

notes.author: user
notes.text: Extend environment configuration with directories and make appropriate profile operations available to agents through MCP.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Implemented the first vertical slice: validated literal per-project environment overrides persisted in SQLite, editable in the dashboard, replaceable through MCP, and injected into shell-free managed process launches. PORT and NODE_ENV are reserved, active servers must be stopped before changes, and audit/log payloads record variable names without values. Named profiles, secret references, env files, working directories, PATH prefixes, required directories, and CLI support remain open.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Extended the literal-variable slice with named per-project profiles. Existing overrides migrate into default; dashboard users can create/copy, edit, select, delete, and save-and-restart profiles, while MCP exposes list/save/select/delete operations. Profile selection persists across worktree switches. Secret references, environment files, working directories, PATH prefixes, required directories, scoped MCP capabilities, and CLI support remain open.

problem: Real development servers often need launch-time feature flags, fixture modes, database guards, or test profiles. Worktree Switcher currently supplies only its own port handling, so projects such as WinPath cannot reproduce an E2E-specific runtime without being started manually.

risk.rollback: Disable custom profiles and fall back to the detected default launch environment. Stored secret references must remain removable without revealing their values.

scope: Add named per-project launch profiles containing validated environment-variable overrides, initially shared by development and optionally scoped separately to production mode.

Support non-secret literal values and secret references resolved from the controller host environment by variable name; do not store secret values in SQLite or return them through HTTP, MCP, audit events, status, errors, or logs.

Allow a profile to select a relative working directory inside the current Git-discovered worktree, which supports applications located in a monorepo subdirectory without accepting an arbitrary child-process cwd.

Allow ordered environment-file references and PATH prefixes. Environment files inside the worktree may be selected by relative path; additional host directories require an explicitly trusted root created by a human and cannot be introduced by an ordinary agent token.

Allow profiles to declare required runtime directories that the controller creates before launch. Creation is confined to the selected worktree, rejects symlink or canonical-path escape, is idempotent, and never implies automatic deletion.
Reserve controller-owned variables including PORT and NODE_ENV so profiles cannot bypass stable-port or runtime-mode policy.

Validate variable names, pass values through the child-process env object with shell:false, display effective variable names and redacted sources, and require a restart when the active profile changes.

Expose profiles through the service layer, dashboard, CLI, and MCP. MCP may read names and redacted effective configuration with project read access, select an existing profile with profiles:select, and create, update, or delete configuration only with a separately granted config:write capability.
Never expose environment-file contents, resolved secret values, or inherited host environment values through MCP. Keep arbitrary executable or free-form shell command input out of scope.
source: Product discussion and WinPath inspection on 2026-08-29
title: Configure safe environment profiles for managed servers
validation: Configure a WinPath-style E2E profile and verify variables such as E2E_RESET_DB_CONFIRM reach the child process while PORT and NODE_ENV remain controller-owned.
Verify a referenced secret is read from the controller environment at launch and never appears in SQLite, API/MCP payloads, logs, errors, or audit records.
Verify invalid variable names, missing required secret references, and attempts to override reserved variables fail before spawning a process.
Verify profile changes require restart, apply to the selected worktree only through its managed process, and preserve shell-free spawning.

Verify relative working directories, environment files, PATH prefixes, and required directories resolve under their approved roots and reject traversal, symlink escape, missing files, and non-directory targets.

Verify an MCP token with profiles:select can choose an existing profile but cannot edit it, while config:write can mutate allowed non-secret configuration and every mutation is attributed and audited.
value: Projects can express development, E2E, fixture, and diagnostic modes without project-specific code in Worktree Switcher or unsafe free-form command execution.
